name: Ashveil Patchskin Thermal Base Layer
description: Hand-stitched from salvaged neoprene strips, scavenged mylar emergency blanket scraps, and repurposed transit-seat foam padding, this Shelf-born thermal underlayer is a monument to desperation engineering. Seams are doubled with whatever thread was available — often mismatched colors, visible and proud. Patchwork panels trap body heat unevenly, creating warm pockets and cold gaps, but it beats bare skin against acid-rain concrete. Smells faintly of industrial solvent no matter how many times it's washed.
functionality: Passive thermal retention through layered salvage materials; no active regulation. Acid-resistant outer surface on select panels from reclaimed chemical-suit fabric. Loose enough to layer over augmentation port housings without snagging.
what_it_says: You survive by your own hands and you've stopped being ashamed of it.
worn_by: Shelf children layered up by parents
story_hooks: A specific patch on the left shoulder is cut from a Tier 4 corporate uniform — someone's going to recognize that logo.
The previous owner stitched a small map into the lining in heat-reactive thread, only visible when the wearer is warm.
A Shelf community elder is the only one who makes them this way — and she just disappeared.
